title: how to create a html button that opens outlook application?
author: Stefan Bogdanescu
excerpt: # The Reality of Launching Outlook from a Web Page You can't simply wrap a standard HTML ` ` element in JavaScript to force the Outlook application to open...
content: # The Reality of Launching Outlook from a Web Page You can't simply wrap a standard HTML ` ``` Here is how the components function: - `outlook:` tells the OS to launch the registered Outlook application. - `?path=/compose/action` directs the app to the compose view. - `&subject=` allows you to pre-fill the subject line. URL encoding (replacing spaces with `%20`) is mandatory for special characters. If you are using Laravel or a PHP-based backend, you might generate this link dynamically: ```php $subject = urlencode('Project Update'); $url = "outlook:?path=/compose/action&subject={$subject}"; // Then pass $url to your view as an href or onclick handler ``` ## The Windows Desktop Environment Constraint A critical pitfall is the assumption that this link will always work. If the user does not have Outlook installed, or if they are using a version of Outlook for Mac, Linux, or a different email client entirely (like Thunderbird), clicking the button will result in a "No application found to handle action" error. Furthermore, some corporate environments restrict the `outlook:` protocol handler for security reasons. If the browser cannot pass control to the registered handler, the link simply fails silently or prompts the user with a generic file dialog. You must account for this failure state in your UI logic, perhaps by falling back to a `mailto:` link if the Outlook launch fails, though that fallback opens a separate mail client rather than the specific Outlook window. ## Handling the "Screenshot" Requirement Your source material mentioned attaching a webpage's screenshot to the email. This introduces a significant complexity because web pages cannot directly access their own rendered DOM state or generate image files from a viewport capture and attach them to an email via a URL scheme without user interaction. The `outlook:` URI scheme is read-only regarding attachments; it can only pre-fill text fields (Subject, Body). It cannot programmatically attach a file generated by the browser's current context. To achieve this, you would need to: 1. Generate the screenshot on the server side before generating the link. 2. Upload that image to a public URL (e.g., an S3 bucket or CDN). 3. Pass the attachment path in the body text as a hyperlink, relying on Outlook to handle inline attachments if they are referenced correctly in the body, or instructing the user to download and attach it manually. Directly injecting binary data or file references into the `outlook:` URI query string is not supported by the Windows Shell or the Outlook application. The most reliable workflow remains generating a static image, hosting it, and providing a link that opens Outlook with the subject line prefilled and a note in the body explaining where to find the screenshot attachment.
